body:
Bind a directory tree to a project with a `.revenuecat.json` holding a `project_id`, found by walking up from the working dir like git finds `.git` (nearest wins).

Precedence, highest first: `--project-id` → `RC_PROJECT_ID` → nearest `.revenuecat.json` → profile default. The binding is a one-shot override like the env vars, so `Save` never bakes a tree-local project into the profile on disk.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how the active project is resolved for every command, so a committed file can silently retarget API calls; malformed files now fail unless a higher override is set.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a commit-able `.revenuecat.json` (`project_id`) discovered by walking up from the working directory (nearest wins). Project resolution is now **`--project-id` > `RC_PROJECT_ID` > dir binding > profile default**.
> 
> The binding is treated as a per-invocation overlay: `Save` reverts it (and env/flag overlays) so a tree-local project is never baked into the profile. Explicit choices go through `UseProjectID`; `--project-id` on ordinary commands uses `OverrideProjectID` (login still adopts the flag as the stored default). Malformed bindings error unless env/flag already wins.
> 
> `projects use` / `create --use` warn (and include `dir_binding_shadow` in `--json`) when a directory file will still override the profile default just set. `profiles list` uses `LoadStored` so it shows on-disk defaults, not overlays.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 498dde70fc287b9c9225901bc4811b823ff7702b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

comments.body:
DX-946 Per-directory project config: bind a folder to a RevenueCat project (upward discovery)

Today account/project selection is **global**: the active profile (`~/.config/revenuecat/.active`) and its `project_id`, overridable only per-invocation via `RC_PROFILE`/`RC_PROJECT_ID`/flags. There's **no per-directory config** — the CLI never looks at your working folder to decide which project you're on. That means a global active profile silently applies in every repo, and people juggling multiple projects across repos must remember to switch (easy to act on the wrong project). Goal: a repo can declare **which RevenueCat project this folder is for**, discovered by walking up from the cwd (like `.nvmrc` / `.tool-versions` / git config / direnv). ## Prior art * **Vercel** `.vercel/` (dir; `orgId`+`projectId`; gitignored), **Netlify** `.netlify/` (dir; gitignored) — per-user link dirs. * **Supabase** `supabase/config.toml`, **Firebase** `.firebaserc`, **Fly** `fly.toml` — committed, non-secret config-as-code; secrets go in gitignored `.env` / env vars. Universal rule: **secrets never committed**; only non-secret pointers/config. ## Design (converged) * **Directory, not a single file:** `.revenuecat/` so we can store more later (project pin now; later cached offering/paywall refs, per-env key hints, etc.). * **Committed pin = project only:** `.revenuecat/project.json` = `{ project_id }` (+ optional human-readable name/slug). **No account/org id** — a project can have collaborators from *different accounts*, so pinning one account would be wrong for every teammate but one. Project IDs are globally unique, so the project pin alone is unambiguous. * **Account resolved per-developer at runtime:** pick **which of *my* logged-in profiles has access to that** `project_id`. Each teammate resolves to their own account automatically. * 0 of my accounts can access it → error: "log into an account with access to (`rc auth login`)". * exactly 1 → use it. * >1 of my own accounts can access it → break the tie with a **per-user, gitignored/global** preference (`project_id → profile`), set once and remembered. **Never committed.** * **Credentials never committed** — stay global per-user. * **Resolution precedence:** `--flag` > `RC_*` env > nearest `.revenuecat/` walking up from cwd > global active profile/project. * `.gitignore` **hygiene:** auto-add any per-user/machine-local bits (e.g. the tie-break preference if stored locally); keep the committed project pin tracked. Mirror Vercel/Netlify's auto-gitignore nicety for the non-committable parts. Why we differ from Vercel (which commits `orgId`): Vercel operates inside one team scope; RevenueCat's cross-account collaborator model makes **project-only pin + runtime "which of my accounts can see it"** the correct resolution. ## Open items to confirm * Efficient "does profile X have access to project_id" check (get-project under each profile) + caching, so resolution isn't slow. * Where the per-user tie-break preference lives (global config keyed by project_id, or a gitignored `.revenuecat/local.json`). * Interaction with `rc projects use` / `rc profiles use` (do those still set globals, and does a folder pin override them? yes, per precedence above). * Whether to warn when the folder pin's project isn't accessible by any logged-in account. ## Related * [DX-940](https://linear.app/revenuecat/issue/DX-940/auth-rc-api-key-env-silently-overrides-interactive-oauth-warn-on) (credential precedence / multi-account) — same subsystem; the folder pin is the "which project" layer on top of profiles.
